title: attn-selection-robustness-probe-and-stability-fixes-for-fa-v3
creator: Marco Liu
description: Investigate a set of stability and tail-latency regressions observed after enabling community FlashAttention v3 for a subset of models. This ticket focuses on (1) probing numerical stability differences between FAv2 and FAv3 under strided/blocked softmax patterns, (2) validating kernel selection heuristics when sequence lengths and kv-cache hit rates vary, and (3) recommending mitigations (runtime patches and scheduling rules) that avoid throughput regressions during prefill/decode transitions.
acceptance_criteria:
- Reproduce at least one P99 regression locally and in canary.
- Produce reproducible microbenchmarks comparing FAv2 vs FAv3 softmax outputs (max absolute and relative diff) across contexts up to 32768 tokens.
- Deliver a short patch or runtime config that removes the regression without >5% throughput loss on target workloads.
- Document changes and submit a reviewable RFC/PR and canary rollout plan.
investigation_steps:
1) Create a deterministic harness to exercise prefill then decode patterns (single-shot long prefill, steady small-step decode, mixed interleaved workloads).
2) Add AVX/FP16/FP32 comparison targets and capture max-abs / mean-abs diffs for softmax outputs between FAv2 and FAv3 builds.
3) Run memory-fragmentation traces while cycling kernels to surface workspace allocation spikes.
4) Force kernel-router to prefer FAv2 for sequences with >4096 tokens and measure tail latency.
5) Test CUDA graph warmup interactions when swapping kernels mid-flight.
6) Verify kv-cache path alignment (strided vs contiguous) for models using rotary embeddings and large head counts.
experiment_results:
- Reproduced 15-30% P99 latency increase on A100S machines for the 64k-context prefill + decode microbenchmark when the kernel router preferred FAv3 kernels under heavy microbatching.
- Numerical comparison: FAv3 softmax (FP16) shows a median max-abs diff of ~1.2e-3 compared to FAv2 for randomly seeded inputs; worst-case drift reached 6.8e-3 on edge-case strided layouts (attention mask with alternating block sparsity).
- Memory analysis: FAv3 kernel code paths created slightly larger temporary workspace peaks in our allocator (~7% larger at peak) due to a different tiling scheme; this increased allocation churn and caused a few spikes in allocation latency under sustained bursts.
- CUDA graphs: when we attempted to cache graph launches that included FAv3 kernels, warmup correctness failures occurred for dynamic sequence lengths. The graphs were only safe when we fixed the workspace size and disallowed variable-shape kernels in graph mode.
tradeoffs_considered:
- Locking kernel-router to FAv2 for long-context requests eliminates regressions but loses some FAv3 throughput gains on typical mid-length traffic.
- Patch softmax numerically (stable exponent normalization) in FAv3 reduces diffs but requires an extra pass in the kernel for certain tiling shapes (cost ~0.5-1% throughput).
- Forcing contiguous kv-cache layout for long prefix workloads simplifies kernel selection but requires additional memcpy on some code paths (memory and latency cost).
proposed_mitigations:
1) Runtime: Add a conservative rule to the kernel-router: prefer FAv2 for prefill when seq_len >= 4096 OR predicted-kv-occupancy >= 80% of workspace.
2) Patch: upstream a small softmax-stabilize fix for strided tiles (PR candidate: github.com/redwood/inference/PR-1142).
3) Scheduling: disable CUDA-graph caching for request shapes that switch between prefill and decode in the same graph; fallback to stream-based launches for those shapes.
4) Observability: add delta-metrics on softmax max-abs-diff and workspace-peak-per-request to the console to catch regressions early.
next_steps:
- Land the softmax-stabilize patch in FAv3 fork and create an opt-in runtime flag (fa_v3_stable_softmax=true).
- Implement kernel-router rule and add integration test that asserts P99 tail latency doesn't regress by >10% on canary.
- Add a job to perf infra that runs the long-context prefill+decode scenario nightly and alerts on delta.
- Schedule a checklist-based canary rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with quick rollback instructions.
